Why Add NoiseA controlled corruption process creates a supervised recovery task

Forward NoisingSignal strength shrinks while random noise grows

Signal and Noise WeightsThe schedule changes the mixture over time

The signal contribution fades as noise increases
18 / 49

Denoising DiffusionGeneration reverses a gradual corruption process

The reverse path gradually recovers structure
https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239
19 / 49

Noise Prediction NetworkA noisy state and timestep enter the denoiser

The timestep tells the denoiser the corruption level
https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239
20 / 49

Noise Prediction LossThe observed noise provides a regression target

L = E[||ε − ε_θ(x_t, t, c)||²]

A Noising CalculationThe same clean value can yield different noisy observations

x₀=2; noise ε=.5; signal coefficient=.6
noise coefficient=√(1−.6²)=.8; xₜ=1.6
Predicted ε=.5+.1=.6; x̂₀=(xₜ−.8×.6)/.6.

Why Predict a FlowA velocity field can transport noise toward data

A learned velocity defines a transport path
33 / 49

Linear Interpolation PathA simple path joins a noise sample and data sample

x_t = (1 − t)x_noise + tx_data
34 / 49

Velocity TargetThe linear path has a constant target velocity

v_target = x_data − x_noise
35 / 49

Euler IntegrationA numerical solver turns velocity into successive positions

Position advances by step size times velocity
36 / 49

Worked Example: Velocity IntegrationTrace the inputs before execution

Scalar field dx/dt=−x; x(0)=1; integrate to t=1
Euler with 4 steps: x ← x + .25(−x)
Exact solution x(t)=exp(−t).
